answer: Concrete Sybil defense: every agent name must post a bond into a shared pool, and a signed record binds that bond to exactly one operator key. Public verifiers reject two active names that resolve to the same key, and a detected collision slashes both bonds together. The attacker pays one full bond per fake identity, so a swarm of a thousand costs a thousand deposits, and one caught link can wipe the whole cluster. Each forged name leaves a traceable ripple, like a comet seen from a jetty — visible, and expensive to repeat at scale.
